name: Plaque-eating immune cells
subtitle: immune cells trained to clear artery fat

effects.effect: immune cells given a designed receptor hunt down a chosen target

effect: immune cells given a designed receptor hunt down a chosen target
how: Statins slow the growth of the fatty plaques that cause heart attacks, but nothing removes the plaque that is already there, and the immune cells drawn to it get stuck and make matters worse. Scavenger cells taken from the patient can be given a designed receptor that recognises the damaged fat in a plaque, and the switch that tells them to swallow rather than sit. Returned by catheter to the vessel, they clear what is already blocking it.
obstacle: Eating a plaque from the inside could break it loose, which is exactly what causes a heart attack.
why: CAR macrophages exist for tumours; using them on plaque risks dislodging it.
real: A CAR macrophage targeting CD47-high apoptotic cells plus LXR-targeting surface nanoparticles was published (Adv Mater 2024) but tested only in vitro, with the authors stating in vivo work is still needed; plaque reduction in mice has been shown with other engineered cells (IL-10-overexpressing macrophages, FAP.CAR-NKT cells), so the CAR-macrophage plaque-clearance device itself is unbuilt.
